scope: Evaluation of livedo reticularis and livedo racemosa.

keyRecommendations.text: Livedo reticularis is a transient or persistent blotchy, reddish-blue to purple, net-like pattern and is described as benign, mainly in middle-aged women.
Livedo racemosa is pathologic and commonly associated with antiphospholipid syndrome.

Every patient needs careful evaluation because of possible systemic disease. Livedo racemosa is the classical sign of Sneddon syndrome and is also seen with APS, SLE, and several prothrombotic diseases.

clinicalBottomLine: Distinguish the benign net-like livedo reticularis from broken, pathologic livedo racemosa, and work up the latter for antiphospholipid syndrome and related systemic disease.
notableCaveats: The review's algorithms are described but not reproduced as a numbered test sequence beyond the diseases it names.
